Everyday needs covered

  • Emergencies and urgent safety — Call 911 for immediate danger and use the linked official service for non-emergency help.
  • Weather and preparedness — Use current National Weather Service information and local emergency alerts.
  • Transit and getting around — Find local transit, parking, road-condition and transportation-assistance sources.
  • Trash, recycling and special waste — Find the right service based on your location and what you need to dispose of.
  • Water, sewer, electricity and gas — Confirm the correct utility provider before taking action; treat a suspected gas leak as an emergency.
  • City services and issue reporting — Choose the right City request type and continue on the official City website.
  • Public records and civic meetings — Find the office that holds the record or the current meeting agenda.
  • Voting and representation — Use official lookups for registration, districts and representatives.
  • Property, taxes and permits — Find the correct office for assessment, deeds, taxes, zoning or permits.
  • Housing help and tenant support — Separate housing-program help, legal help, counseling and fair-housing resources.
  • Food, bills and basic-needs help — Find immediate local help and official benefit-application resources.
  • Health and public-health services — Find official health-service starting points without diagnosis or treatment advice.
  • Mental-health and crisis support — Keep 988 and 911 easy to reach when urgent support is needed.
  • Domestic-violence help — Provide discreet safety resources without collecting a private story.
  • Children, child care and parenting — Find official child-care and family-support resources without endorsing a provider.
  • Schools and school-day logistics — Keep Franklin Special District and Williamson County Schools separate and use their address-specific tools.
  • Older adults and disability services — Find services by need, accessibility and eligibility.
  • Library, learning and internet access — Find public library, internet, education and training resources.
  • Jobs and workforce help — Find official job openings and training resources without promising employment.
  • Parks, trails and recreation — Check facilities, accessibility, registration, hours and closures.
  • Events and things to do — Use current event pages and confirm details before making plans.
  • New-resident orientation — Start with an overview, then continue to the agency that owns each service.

Events, weather, transit, hours, eligibility, availability and emergency information can change quickly. This page links to current sources but does not make live-status promises. Call 911 for immediate danger; call or text 988 for a mental-health crisis.
